subject: Re: VPC connectivity + IP allowlist — next steps and SDK/auth follow-up
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@finpay.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Initial VPC notes and follow-up items

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call today — helpful to see how Redwood handles private deployments. As promised, attaching a simple VPC diagram and our topline network/security constraints. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- We plan to use AWS in us-west-2.
- Primary requirement: Redwood Private must be reachable only from our VPC via an interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) or via private peering; public egress is a blocker.
- We need an IP allowlist for control-plane callbacks and webhook URLs. Can you confirm which IPs or ranges we should expect?
- mTLS for admin/agent connections is preferred; if Redwood supports client certs for the private control plane, that would be great.
- DNS: our egress/DNS must resolve model registry endpoints privately; does Redwood support configuring private hosted zones / Route53 resolver rules?

Next steps: send whatever artifacts you need (our VPC CIDRs, security group changes). Could you also summarize SDK auth options (API key vs mTLS) and recommended routing for embeddings/rekanker traffic?

Best,
Alice
Director, Platform Engineering
FinPay

Attachments: finpay_vpc_diagram.png (image/png)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@finpay.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial VPC notes and follow-up items

Thanks Alice — good notes. Quick recap from our side and recommended next steps.

Recap / Redwood capabilities:
- Private connectivity: Redwood Private supports both AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints) and customer-managed peering depending on account requirements. For most customers, we recommend PrivateLink because it avoids routing table changes and NAT.
- IP allowlist: Control plane callbacks (webhooks, health checks) come from a set of stable ranges; we will provide specific CIDRs from our infra team in the follow-up. For Dedicated/Private customers we can also configure static egress NAT IPs on request.
- Auth: SDKs support two patterns — API key bearer tokens (short-lived recommended via your KMS) and mTLS client certs for the control-plane agent. For sensitive environments we recommend mTLS + RBAC on the control plane and short-lived API tokens for app calls.
- DNS/egress: We support Route53 resolver rules and private hosted zones for model registry resolution. If you need outbound calls to external indexing/embedding service, we can route through a customer-managed NAT or use our egress proxy with mTLS.
- Routing: Per-route model routing is configured in the Console; for low-latency embedding/reranking we recommend colocating embedding calls to the same region as the model host and using our streaming SDK to reduce connection churn.

Immediate next steps (what we need from you):
1) VPC CIDR ranges, subnets you want to use for interface endpoints.
2) Proxy/NAT preference (do you require customer-managed NAT or allow Redwood-managed egress IPs?).
3) Whether you want admin agent to use mTLS or rely on API keys.
4) A short list of routes that need to go via private endpoints (model registry, embeddings, metrics).

I’ll loop our infra lead (Jonas) to provide the CIDR ranges and the temporary IP allowlist. I’ve attached a Redwood integration checklist and high-level diagram.

— Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_private_integration_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finpay.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial VPC notes and follow-up items

Hi Alice — looping in technical details for the network team.

IP ranges (temporary for testing):
- 52.34.120.0/22
- 34.210.16.0/21
(These are our staging egress ranges; production ranges will be provided via a signed config sheet.)

PrivateLink setup notes:
- Create interface endpoints in the subnets you designate (AZ-aware).
- Point your Route53 private hosted zone to resolve our internal hostnames (we will provide zone names).
- For mTLS: we will accept client certs signed by your internal CA; send us the CSR or the CA bundle and we will whitelist the client certificate fingerprint on the control plane.

SDK/auth guidance:
- For server-to-server embedding calls we recommend short-lived API tokens minted by your identity system (rotate every 24h) — lower operational complexity.
- For control-plane agent connections (agent used for private model pulls, metrics), use mTLS with mutual verification.

Notes on embeddings/rerankers:
- If you plan to run reranking locally, push embeddings to your vector store and call Redwood for generation only; otherwise use our embedding endpoints pinned to private endpoints to avoid egress to public internet.
- For high-throughput rerankers, enable connection pooling in the SDK (we have a Node/Python option) and configure batching in the Console.

Let me know a time if you want a short runbook call to walk through the PrivateLink creation steps.

— Jonas
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

- We will create interface endpoints in three subnets across AZs a/b/c.

- For mTLS: we can issue a CA-signed cert for the control-plane agent. Next question: what is the recommended validity period for client certs? Is short-lived (30d) OK?

Also, would you be able to provide a sample Terraform snippet for the endpoint + route53 setup? That would speed things up on our side.
